problem: VLN-CE methods based on MLLMs or fidelity-oriented world models keep excessive task-irrelevant perceptual detail. Global Q-Former attention lets instruction cues get diluted by visual noise, which hurts generalization and adds computation.
motivation: Sparse symbolic instructions and dense visual observations differ greatly in entropy, so instruction cues get overwhelmed. World models that reconstruct fine detail (texture, lighting) overfit and are costly. The paper applies a 'Minimal Sufficiency' principle: keep only the information needed for action.
key_idea: Filter perception with instruction-conditioned queries (Focus-Former), compress the latent world state with a learned CP low-rank factorization (MCA), and run a world model over the factorized latent space (CWM).
insight: Ablations show the gains come from compression and task-driven structure rather than reconstruction fidelity. Removing the reconstruction loss costs only 2% SR, while removing posterior-prior matching costs 5% SR. Removing MCA doubles runtime (236s to 516s). Replacing the Focus-Former with a Q-Former drops NE from 4.36 to 4.85. The CP rank peaks at R=16, and perturbing the CP factors hurts performance, with random replacement worse than zeroing.
method: Logical Anchor Model / Focus-Former: a two-stage cascaded attention. Learnable queries first attend to instruction features (logic anchoring), then the anchored queries attend to observation features (task-driven selection). The output goes to Qwen2.5-VL-7B together with the instruction features to produce the latent Z.

Minimalist Constraint Alignment (MCA): a shallow MLP (2 hidden layers of width 128, with a CNN prior) predicts CP factors u, v, w of rank R=16 from Z. The compact Ẑ is rebuilt as a sum of rank-one outer products, reducing complexity from O(NMD) to O(R(N+M+D)).

Compression World Model (CWM): an RSSM-style latent simulator with a posterior and a prior transition network over the CP factors. It rolls out T_p=2 future steps, and the predicted actions serve as a prior for the final decision.

Phase I training: CWM is trained with a variational objective (reconstruction, action prediction, KL posterior-prior match). The Focus-Former is trained with an IB objective, instantiated as an L1 sparsity penalty on the CP factors (L_LMM).
Phase II training: end-to-end co-evolution with L = L_WM + λ1 L_LMM + λ2 L_PO + L_IL. L_PO = ||Z-Ẑ||² is the predictive offset loss and L_IL is the imitation loss, with λ1=8e-3 and λ2=1e-3.
Backbone and setup: built on the ETPNav/HNR pipeline with a CLIP ViT-B/32 RGB encoder and a ResNet50 depth encoder. Trained for 10K episodes on R2R-CE and 20K on RxR-CE.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (MLLM) + Focus-Former + CP-MLP + RSSM-style CWM, on an ETPNav/HNR-style graph planner (CLIP ViT-B/32, ResNet50 depth)
setting.training_data: R2R-CE train (10K episodes) and RxR-CE train (20K episodes), starting from ETPNav pretrained initialization; no extra synthetic data mentioned
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints on a topological map, mapped to low-level control

numbers.evidence: Table 1 (Results on R2R-CE), Val Unseen columns

numbers.extra: online VLN setting; avg 236s per instruction

numbers_note: The R2R-CE/RxR-CE tables print integer SR/SPL for most rows. The abstract's 2.0/1.0 gain corresponds to 66/54 vs NavMorph (HNR) 64/53 on val-unseen.
results: CompactNav reaches 66 SR / 54 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, beating NavMorph (HNR) at 64/53, and 63 SR / 55 SPL on test-unseen vs 60/52. On RxR-CE val-unseen it reaches 58.96 SR / 49.76 SPL vs NavMorph's 58.02/48.98. Inference time is comparable to NavMorph (236s vs 227s).
limitations: Performance depends on anchoring quality and the low-rank bottleneck; the CP rank is fixed (R=16), so adaptive rank selection is future work.
The MLLM backbone adds computational overhead.
Evaluated only in simulation on R2R-CE/RxR-CE; the theoretical 'proofs' rest on idealized assumptions (the IB is a practical L1 surrogate), and gains over NavMorph are small (1-2 points).
